title: Man vs zone
summary: The two ways to cover receivers, and how to tell which one the defense is playing.

steps.text: There are two ways to cover a pass. In man coverage, each defender picks one receiver and follows him wherever he goes. It is like a game of tag: you have one person and you stay with him.

In zone coverage, each defender guards an area of the field instead of a person. If a receiver runs into your zone, you cover him. If he leaves, you pass him to the next defender. Watch how the linebackers drop to spots on this play.
How do you tell? Watch a defender at the snap. If he turns his back to the quarterback and runs with a receiver, it is man. If he keeps his eyes on the quarterback and drops to a spot, it is zone.
Each has a weakness. Man coverage can be beaten by a faster receiver, or by two receivers crossing so the defenders bump into each other. That is what Mesh does.

Zone coverage has holes between the zones. Smart receivers sit down in those holes, like a curl right between two defenders. Offenses attack man with crossing routes and attack zone by finding the gaps.

quiz.prompt: In man coverage, what does each defender do?
choices: Guards one area of the field
Follows one receiver wherever he goes
quiz.explanation: Man means one defender on one receiver, like tag.

quiz.prompt: In zone coverage, what does each defender do?
choices: Guards one area of the field
quiz.explanation: Zone defenders guard spots on the field and pass receivers along.

quiz.prompt: A cornerback turns his back to the quarterback and runs with the receiver. What coverage is that?
quiz.explanation: Turning and running with a receiver is a man coverage sign.

quiz.prompt: Which play is designed to beat man coverage by making defenders bump into each other?
quiz.explanation: Mesh crosses two receivers close together so the defenders chasing them collide.

quiz.prompt: What is the weakness of zone coverage?
quiz.explanation: Receivers can sit down in the holes between zones.
